sources.label: DHS OIG, Jan 2026
sources.html: CTMS "has not met its original goal to help recruit thousands of cyber experts," with only several hundred hired since 2021 launch — against an original estimate of 2,000 hires.
sources.context: The OPM series in this report peaks at {peak_headcount} people in {peak_month_label}.

check.claim: Hiring fell short of the 2,000-hire estimate ("several hundred")
check.note: OPM counts only the cyber-series DC/DL population defined in this report; the OIG figure may use a broader definition.

sources.label: Hysen testimony, Jun 26 2024
sources.html: DHS CIO, House Homeland Security Committee: "We are pushing to aggressively expand CTMS." Also: "our initial rate of hires have not met our aggressive targets."
sources.context: The OPM series peaks {peak_timing_vs_testimony}, then changes {peak_to_latest_pct_label} from that peak through {last_month_label}.

sources.label: Appropriations
sources.html: $49M (FY16–20) design/build funding, plus $93.2M enacted Mar 15, 2022 (Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2022) to launch hiring for 65 positions. A House Homeland Security member has separately referenced Congress rescinding ~$53M over slow CISA hiring.
sources.caveat: The rescission's date and citation are not yet pinned to primary text.

sources.label: A claim worth watching
sources.html: DHS publicly cited a "94% two-year retention rate" in mid-2024.
sources.foot: Cross-checked using maturity-eligible individual timelines in this report

check.note: Cohort, date, and definition differences may explain some of the gap.

sources.label: Primary-verified: OIG-25-38, Sep 11 2025
sources.html: A related-but-separate program: CISA "did not properly design, implement, comply with, or manage" its Cybersecurity Retention Incentive (CRI) — $138M paid FY2020–24, incentives given to ineligible staff, no recipient records kept, $1.41M in improper back-payments to 348 people.
sources.caveat: CISA has said (per press reporting, not this PDF) it is ending CRI because CTMS is meant to absorb that function; this report does not independently confirm that transition.

link.text: Primary source: full OIG report PDF

sources.label: Context for 2025's decline
sources.html: CISA's total workforce fell to ~2,400 by Dec 2025 (down ~29% since early 2025), following DOGE-driven contract cancellations (300+ election-security and red-team staff cut in Mar 2025) and mass departures — Axios reported a third of CISA's top cyber talent gone by Jun 2025.
